title: CI never runs any test — add a check workflow
description:
PROBLEM
`.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml` is the ONLY workflow. It builds and releases on push to main and runs no tests at all. So `rookery-search/0.2.0`s `just parity` — the single thing keeping the Typst and JavaScript copies of the ranking rule from drifting — has never run in CI, and nothing checks that a package still compiles. The root `Justfile` walks nested Justfiles running `just` (the DEFAULT recipe), which for rookery-search is `build`, not `parity`, so a repo-wide `just build` does not run it either.

STEPS
1. Add `.github/workflows/check.yml`, on `push` and `pull_request`, mirroring publish-packages.ymls setup steps (`actions/checkout@v5`, `pnpm/action-setup@v5`, `actions/setup-node@v5` node 22, `extractions/setup-just@v3`) plus a typst install (pin the version in `rookery*/typst.toml`s `compiler` field, 0.15.0 floor; 0.15.1 is what this repo is developed against).
2. Run, at minimum:
   - `cd rookery-search/0.2.0 && just build && just parity`
   - `cd rookery/0.2.0 && just test` (see the rookery unit-test bead; skip this step until that lands)
   - compile both rookery demos, which is this repos definition of "lint" (CLAUDE.md, "Build"):
     `cd rookery/0.2.0/demo/pure && mkdir -p build && typst compile --features html --format html --root ../.. root.typ build/root.html && typst compile --features html --root ../.. paged.typ build/paged.pdf`
3. Do NOT fold these into publish-packages.yml — a release run must not be gated on a demo, and a PR needs the checks before merge.

VERIFY
Push a branch with `fuzzy-score`s `+10` prefix bonus changed to `+11` in `rookery-search/0.2.0/src/lib.typ` and confirm the workflow fails on `just parity`. Revert.

title: Duplicated and stale comment blocks in rookery lib.typ
description:
PROBLEM
Three blocks of commentary in `rookery/0.2.0/src/lib.typ` exist twice. In a file whose comments are the packages design record, a duplicate is worse than in ordinary code: the next person to correct one has no way to know the other is there, and the two then disagree about the same decision.

1. Lines 1672-1706 (above `#window`) are a near-verbatim re-paste of lines 1005-1036 (above `_window-content`) — the "ONE rendering, whatever `folded` says" paragraph, the whole "CLICK BUDGET (HTML/EPUB)" section including the Forester `tree.xsl` reference, the `<details>`/`<summary>` paragraph, and the `show-date` paragraph. Confirmed by grep: `CLICK BUDGET` at :1009 and :1679, `The disclosure is native` at :1026 and :1696, `show-date` is OFF by default` at :1032 and :1702.
2. Inside `_window-content`, lines 1074-1077 and 1090-1091 both say "`shown`, not the untruncated body — the caller already applied `limit:`", about the same two expressions on the same line.
3. `rookery-search/0.2.0/test/parity.typ:44` says the `body-parity` fixture is "Consumed by the JS ports own parity bead, not by `test/parity.mjs` here". It is: `test/parity.mjs:39` reads `<body-parity>` and diffs it. The comment was true when written and is now misleading about what enforces what.

STEPS
1. Keep the CLICK BUDGET / `<details>` / `show-date` material at `_window-content` (:1005-1036) — that is the function that renders it. Cut it from above `#window` and leave a one-line pointer there instead: `#window`s own comment should cover its ARGUMENTS (`names`, `tags`, `match`, `sort`, `depth`), which is material the other copy does not have.
2. Collapse the two `shown` paragraphs in `_window-content` into one.
3. Fix the `parity.typ:44` comment to say `test/parity.mjs` consumes it. If the tiering-parity bead lands first, that bead already fixes this line — check before duplicating the edit.
4. No code changes. Confirm by diff that only comment lines moved.

VERIFY
`grep -c "CLICK BUDGET" src/lib.typ` returns 1. `demo/pure` still compiles (it must, but compile it anyway — a stray character in a comment block that spans a `#let` is easy to make).

title: Three verbatim copies of the limit: truncation block
description:
PROBLEM
`rookery/0.2.0/src/lib.typ` repeats the same five-line block-truncation snippet three times, character for character apart from variable names:

  - `_flatten`s WK expansion rule, :1242-1247
  - `#window`, :1813-1818
  - `#idea-body`, :1921-1926

    let bs = _blocks(body)
    let shown = if limit != none and bs.len() > limit {
      bs.slice(0, limit).join() + [#text(gray)[ ... ]]
    } else { body }

This is the one place the package breaks its own rule. Half a dozen comments in this file explain that an affordance is factored out precisely "so the two cannot drift" — `_permalink` (:361), `_window-content` (:989), `_resolve-dest` (:349), `_note-file` (:306). The ellipsis is presentation and the block unit is semantics, and both are currently spelled out three times.

The same defect in smaller form: `_note-href` (:339-347) and `_page-href` (:2360-2370) each compute the depth prefix independently —
  `let depth = <handle>.split(":").len() - 1`
  `let prefix = if depth == 0 { "" } else { range(depth).map(x => "../").join() }`
— identical arithmetic against a note id in one and a spine handle in the other.

STEPS
1. Add `_truncate(body, limit)` returning the body unchanged when `limit == none` or the body has no more blocks than the limit, and the truncated join plus the ellipsis otherwise. Define it next to `_blocks` (above `_flatten`, which needs it — closures capture at definition time). Replace all three call sites.
2. Add `_rel-prefix(handle)` returning `""` or `n × "../"`, and have both `_note-href` and `_page-href` call it.
3. Pure moves, no behaviour change. Note that `limit: 0` currently yields `().join()` -> `none` plus the ellipsis, which renders as a bare "…"; keep that exactly as it is here and let the limit-validation bead decide whether it should be an error.

VERIFY
`demo/pure` compiles to HTML and PDF unchanged, and a `#window(.., limit: 1)` case still truncates. If the demo-coverage bead has landed, its `limit:` case covers this directly.

title: demo/pure exercises only a quarter of the package
description:
PROBLEM
`rookery/0.2.0/demo/pure/` is the only thing in this repo that compiles the package, and between `a.typ`, `b.typ` and `paged.typ` it touches exactly: `#idea` (named and auto), `#window` with no arguments, `#hyperlink`, `#show ref: hyperlink`, and the paged branch. Everything else in a 2753-line package compiles for the first time in a users project.

NOT EXERCISED ANYWHERE IN-REPO
- `#footnote` — including the `panic` at lib.typ:1414 when a Typst `#footnote` is used inside an idea without importing rookerys, and the document-wide fallback for a footnote written outside any idea.
- `bibliography:` — the per-idea References block, the sweep block for prose citations before an idea, and the trailing-prose block at lib.typ:2743. The comment at :1524 records that a citation with no bibliography is a HARD ERROR on the paged target, so the paged demo is exactly where this needs to compile.
- `#ideas-outline` — both forms, `depth:`, and `title: none`.
- `#note`/`#todo`/`tags:`/`#tags-of`, and `#window(tags: .., match: "all")`.
- `#idea-body`.
- `#window` with `limit:`, `folded:`, `show-date:`, `sort:`, `depth:` — `_blocks` truncation in particular, whose `styled`-unwrap regression (:959) silently disabled `limit:` for every note and would not have been caught by anything here.
- `#show: rookery.with(prefix: ..)` — the whole `_pfx` story, four readers that must agree.
- `theme:` and the granular colour parameters.
- A self-window and an A-windows-B/B-windows-A cycle — the termination argument at :1113 is the packages most load-bearing claim and nothing compiles it.

STEPS
1. Extend `demo/pure/` with one file per cluster above (`footnotes.typ`, `bib.typ` + a small `refs.bib`, `outline.typ`, `tags.typ`, `windows.typ`, `theme.typ`, `cycles.typ`) and `#include` them from `root.typ`.
2. `prefix:` and `theme:` need their own root, since both are document-wide: add `root-prefix.typ` rather than folding them into `root.typ`.
3. Where a case is meant to FAIL (the Typst-footnote panic), do not put it in the compiled demo — note it in a comment and cover it in the unit-test bead if `assert`-style negative testing is feasible, or leave it to the readme.
4. Add each new compile target to `demo/pure/Justfile` and to the CI check workflow.

VERIFY
Every root in `demo/pure/` compiles to both HTML and PDF with `--features html`. Revert the `styled` unwrap in `_blocks` and confirm the `limit:` case in `windows.typ` visibly stops truncating.

title: panic at lib.typ:1455 lacks the package prefix and the useful detail
description:
PROBLEM
`rookery/0.2.0/src/lib.typ:1455`:

    panic("rookery: duplicate note id " + id)

Every other diagnostic in the package opens with `@rheo/rookery:` — the other three panics at :885, :1785 and :1917, and all fourteen asserts. This one does not, so the one message an author is most likely to hit while writing (two `#idea("same-name")` calls) is the one that does not identify which package produced it.

It is also the least informative of the four. The registry record it just compared holds `origin` — the handle of the vertebra each note was written in — so the message can name both sides. A duplicate id in a rookery spread over dozens of files is otherwise a hunt: the panic names the id and nothing about where either note lives.

Note the check is deliberately narrow and must stay so: an IDENTICAL re-insertion is a re-emission, not a collision (see the comment at :1401), so only a genuine mismatch panics.

FIX
    panic(
      "@rheo/rookery: duplicate note id " + id + " — already registered"
        + (if existing.origin != none { " in " + existing.origin } else { "" })
        + ", registered again" + (if origin != none { " in " + origin } else { "" })
        + ". A pinned id must be unique across the whole rookery.",
    )

reading `r.at(id)` into `existing` before the comparison. Keep it robust when either `origin` is `none` — that is the plain `typst compile` case, where nothing publishes a handle.

VERIFY
Two `#idea("dup")[..]` calls in different files of `demo/pure` fail with a message naming the package, the id, and both files handles. Two identical `#idea("same")` re-emissions still do not panic.

title: #window/#idea-body: limit: is the one parameter with no assert
description:
PROBLEM
Every other parameter on `#window` (`rookery/0.2.0/src/lib.typ:1707`) validates its argument and fails with a `@rheo/rookery:` message naming the call site: `depth` (:1717), `tags` (:1722), `match` (:1729), `sort` (:1734), the positional count (:1743). `limit:` validates nothing.

MEASURED, typst 0.15.1:
  `#window("multi", limit: "2")` ->
    error: cannot compare integer and string
       lib.typ:1814:37  if limit != none and bs.len() > limit
  An error inside the package, pointing at package source, for a mistake made at the call site.

  `#window("multi", limit: -1)` -> compiles, silently renders no body at all and a bare "…", because `bs.slice(0, -1)` drops the last element and a negative index is legal. `limit: 0` likewise renders only the ellipsis.

`#idea-body` (:1913) has the same hole in both `limit:` and `depth:` — it validates neither, though `#window` asserts `depth` and the two take the same budget.

STEPS
1. In `#window`, beside the existing asserts, add:
     assert(
       limit == none or (type(limit) == int and limit >= 1),
       message: "@rheo/rookery: #windows `limit` must be none or a positive "
         + "integer (the number of leading blocks to show) — got " + repr(limit),
     )
   `>= 1` rather than `>= 0`: a window showing nothing but an ellipsis is not a truncation of anything, and `limit: 0` reads as a mistake, not a request.
2. Add the same assert to `#idea-body`, plus the `depth` assert `#window` already carries (:1717) — copy it verbatim so the two messages agree.
3. Mention the rule in the readmes `limit:` documentation.

VERIFY
`#window("x", limit: "2")`, `limit: 0` and `limit: -1` each fail with the packages own message naming the parameter; `limit: none` and `limit: 2` behave exactly as before. Cover the valid cases in `demo/pure` if that bead has landed.

title: .marrow.typ imports 15 internals with no declared boundary
description:
PROBLEM
`rookery/0.2.0/.marrow.typ:72` imports fifteen names from `@rheo/rookery:0.2.0`, fourteen of them underscore-private:

  _registry, _note-file, _pfx, _permalink, _themed, _handle-title, _page-links,
  _page-href, _body-at, _footnoted, _refs-block, _own-cited-keys,
  _window-depth, _idea-page-template, _IDEA-DIR, window

That is a substantial internal API with no marker on either side. Nothing in lib.typ says these fifteen are load-bearing for a second file, so a refactor renaming or re-signing any of them looks local and is not — and the failure mode is unusually bad. Per the note in `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml`, rheos `package_marrow_source` returns None for a missing marrow rather than erroring, so a broken marrow does not fail the build loudly; and CLAUDE.md records that a `.marrow.typ` mistake leaves a package that "installs, compiles, and simply mints none of the pages it exists to mint".

The upcoming pure-helper extraction makes this concrete: `_footnoted`, `_refs-block` and `_own-cited-keys` all sit in the region that gets moved around.

STEPS
1. In lib.typ, add one banner section — "CONSUMED BY .marrow.typ" — listing the fifteen names, each with one line on what marrow uses it for, and stating plainly that changing a name or signature requires changing `.marrow.typ` in the same commit. Put it near the top, where a reader lands, not buried beside one of the functions.
2. Do NOT move the definitions to satisfy the banner; several of them (`_footnoted`, `_body-at`) are ordering-sensitive where they are.
3. Consider whether the list can shrink. `_IDEA-DIR` + `_note-file` + `_pfx` are used by marrow only to rebuild the handle `ideas:<slug>` and the slug itself — a single `_note-page(id)` returning `(file: .., handle: .., slug: ..)` would replace three imports with one, and would put the path/handle mirroring that lib.typ:306-321 already worries about in one function instead of split across two files.
4. Add the check to the CI workflow: `typst compile` a rheo demo that mints pages (see the rheo-demo bead) is the only thing that actually proves marrow still works.

VERIFY
The banner names exactly the set `.marrow.typ` imports — diff the two lists mechanically, e.g. `grep -o "_[a-z-]*" .marrow.typ:72 | sort -u` against the banner. If step 3 is taken, minting still produces the same paths and handles.

title: wireModal's limit fallback disagrees with #search-modal's default
description:
PROBLEM
`rookery-search/0.2.0/src/rookery-search.js:497`:

    const limit = Number(dialog.dataset.rookerySearchLimit || "8");

The fallback is 8, which is `#search-bar`s default (`src/lib.typ:315`). `#search-modal`s default is 30 (`src/lib.typ:416`), and the line was copied from `wire` (:234), where 8 is correct. The two are different UIs with different amounts of room — a dropdown under an input against a full-height overlay pane — which is why the Typst side gives them different defaults.

It is latent rather than active: `#search-modal` always emits `data-rookery-search-limit`, so the fallback only fires for a dialog assembled by hand or by a site building its own markup on this script — a supported use, per the modules "the global is what lets a site build its own UI on this ranking" (:11).

FIX
Change the fallback to `"30"` and add a short comment naming `#search-modal`s default as the source of the number, so the next reader does not "tidy" it back into agreement with `wire`.

VERIFY
Remove `data-rookery-search-limit` from a dialog by hand in a built page and confirm the modal shows up to 30 rows.

title: Parity fixture is 23 hand-written cases — add generated cases
description:
PROBLEM
`rookery-search/0.2.0/test/parity.typ` pins the two scorers with 17 + 6 hand-picked cases. Every one was added in response to a defect already found, which means the fixture is a regression suite, not a search for drift. The two implementations are in different languages with different string models — Typst `.clusters()` vs a JS spread, `str.position` (bytes) vs `indexOf` (UTF-16), the `-`/`_` folding on both sides — and those are precisely the places a hand-written table will not think to look.

STEPS
1. Generate cases in `test/parity.mjs` from a FIXED seed (no `Math.random()` without one — a failure has to be reproducible), drawing from an alphabet that includes: ASCII words, `-`/`_`, mixed case, combining-mark sequences, an emoji with a ZWJ, and CJK. Queries drawn as substrings, subsequences, and near-misses of the hay.
2. Write the generated cases into a temp `.typ` next to `parity.typ` that imports `/src/lib.typ` and emits `#metadata(..) <generated>`, then `typst eval` it exactly as `evalMetadata` already does, and diff.
3. On a mismatch, print the case in a form that can be pasted straight into `parity.typ` as a permanent regression case — the generated suite finds drift, the hand-written one keeps it fixed.
4. A few hundred cases per run is plenty; keep the runtime under a couple of seconds so CI can afford it on every push.

CONTEXT
`_fold` deliberately does NOT accent-fold (lib.typ:52, "cafe" does not match "Café") and that asymmetry is documented as a limitation — a generated case hitting it is CORRECT behaviour on both sides and must agree, not be excluded.

VERIFY
`just parity` runs the generated suite and passes. Change `body-score`s earliness bucket from 200 to 199 in the Typst copy only and confirm a generated case catches it.

title: Parity test does not cover the tiering rule (search-ideas vs search)
description:
PROBLEM
The ranking rule is implemented TWICE by design — `search-ideas` in `rookery-search/0.2.0/src/lib.typ:178` and `search` in `src/rookery-search.js:96` — and `just parity` only diffs the two LEAF scorers (`fuzzy-score`/`score`, `body-score`/`bodyScore`). The layer above them is duplicated and unchecked:

  - which tier a row lands in (name = better of id-score and title-score, else body);
  - `text == ""` skipping the title score;
  - every name-tier row sorting above every body-tier row;
  - tie-breaking (Typst leans on `ideas()` id-order plus a stable sort; JS sorts explicitly by `a.id < b.id`);
  - `limit` applied to the CONCATENATION, not per tier;
  - JS treating a missing `row.body` as `""` (:107) where Typst uses `e.at("body", default: "")` (:201).

Those are exactly the parts most likely to drift, and a drift is silent: the static Typst listing and the live bar simply disagree about ordering.

STEPS
1. In `rookery-search/0.2.0/test/parity.typ` add a THIRD fixture, `<tier-parity>`: a hand-built array of note rows shaped like `ideas()` output (`id, name, text, body`) plus a list of queries. For each query, emit the ordered result of running the tiering rule over those rows.
   `search-ideas` reads `ideas()` (a `state`) and so cannot be called on a literal corpus. Either (a) refactor `search-ideas` to take the rows as an optional parameter defaulting to `ideas()`, keeping the public signature intact, or (b) extract the pure part as `_rank(rows, query, limit)` and have `search-ideas` call it — (b) is preferred and mirrors how the JS side is already shaped.
2. Emit `(query, ids: (..), scores: (..), kinds: (..))` per case — ORDER is the thing under test, so compare the id sequence, not a set.
3. In `test/parity.mjs`, read `<tier-parity>` the same way the other two are read and diff against `search(rows, query, limit)` from `../src/rookery-search.js`, reporting the first differing index.
4. Include cases that actually exercise the boundaries: a note matching on title only; one matching on body only; two name-tier rows tying on score (id order); a body-tier row with a higher raw score than a name-tier row (must still sort below it); a row with `text: ""`; a row with no `body` key at all; `limit` cutting across the tier boundary.
5. Fix the stale comment at `test/parity.typ:44` while there — it says the `body-parity` fixture is "Consumed by the JS ports own parity bead, not by `test/parity.mjs` here", but `parity.mjs:39` does consume it.

VERIFY
`cd rookery-search/0.2.0 && just parity` reports three OK lines. Then flip the JS tier comparator to `tier(b) - tier(a)` and confirm it fails.

title: rookery: no in-repo coverage of the rheo-only half
Extract lib.typ's pure leaf helpers into their own module
description:
PROBLEM
`rookery/0.2.0/src/lib.typ` is a single 2753-line file (roughly 800 lines of code under 1900 of commentary) holding everything from `sys.inputs` reads to a footnote engine to an outline builder. It is navigable only by its section banners, and its ordering is load-bearing in a way the file itself has to keep explaining: at least six comments say a helper is "defined HERE" because a Typst `#let` closure captures the scope visible AT DEFINITION time.

A subset of it does not participate in that at all. These helpers touch no `state`, no `context`, no `query` and no target detection — they are pure functions over strings and content:

  `_norm` (:419), `_dedup-tag` (:1558), `_tag-pred` (:438), `_sort-ids` (:1612),
  `_blocks` (:970), `_join` (:2410), `_plain` (:2384), `_body-text` (:2412),
  `_body-plain` (:2435), `_nest-outline` (:2243), `_cite-walk` (:249),
  `_footnotes` (:501), `_std-footnotes` (:539)

Pulled out, they can be imported and tested directly, and lib.typ loses its least interesting third.

STEPS
1. Land the rookery unit-test bead FIRST so the move is verified rather than hoped at.
2. Create `rookery/0.2.0/src/pure.typ` holding those functions and their comments verbatim. `IK`/`WK`/`FNK` (lib.typ:456, :457, :478) are plain constants the walkers compare against — move them there too, since `_footnotes`/`_std-footnotes`/`_cite-walk` need them and lib.typ can re-export.
3. In lib.typ, replace the definitions with one `#import "pure.typ": *` near the top. A relative import inside a package resolves against the packages own directory and is safe here — unlike in `.marrow.typ`, whose text is spliced into rheos bundle root (see that files header).
4. Keep the names, including the leading underscore, and keep them exported from lib.typ: `.marrow.typ` imports internals from `"@rheo/rookery:0.2.0"` by name, and `test/units.typ` will too.
5. Do NOT move anything reading `_prefix`, `_theme`, `_registry`, `_bib`, `_window-depth`, `_idea-page-template`, `state("rheo-handle")` or `_target()`. That is the ordering-sensitive core and splitting it is a separate, riskier question — explicitly out of scope here.

VERIFY
`just test`, both `demo/pure` compiles, and `just parity` in rookery-search (which imports `ideas`/`note-href` across the package boundary) all still pass. `wc -l src/lib.typ` drops by roughly 400.

title: rookery: unit-test fixture for the pure helpers
description:
GOAL
`rookery/0.2.0/src/lib.typ` is 2753 lines and has ZERO automated tests. Its pure, state-free helpers each carry a MEASURED regression recorded in a comment; nothing pins any of them. Add a Typst-side assertion fixture plus a `just test` recipe.

THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS REPO
`rookery-search/0.2.0/test/parity.typ` + `test/parity.mjs` show it: a fixture `.typ` imports internals by relative path (`#import "/src/lib.typ": fuzzy-score`), emits results as `#metadata(..) <label>`, and a runner reads them with
`typst eval --features html --root . --format json "query(<label>).first().value" --in test/fixture.typ`.
Here no JS is needed: the fixture can `assert.eq` directly and `typst compile` it, so a failure is a non-zero exit with a line number.

STEPS
1. Create `rookery/0.2.0/test/units.typ`. `#import "/src/lib.typ": ..` the helpers below (they are underscore-private, which is fine — `.marrow.typ` already imports internals the same way).
2. Cover at least these, one `assert.eq` per case, each named in a comment by the defect it pins:
   - `_norm` (lib.typ:419) — bare name, full id, `label`, and a name containing a second `:`.
   - `_dedup-tag` (:1558) — the `#todo("x", tags: ("todo",))` -> `("todo",)` case named in its comment.
   - `_join` (:2410) — empty array returns `""`, not `none` (the MEASURED crash at :2404).
   - `_plain` (:2384) — a title containing `raw` must NOT flatten to a double space (the MEASURED "The  marker" defect at :2379).
   - `_body-text`/`_body-plain` (:2412, :2435) — a `parbreak` and an `item` must emit a boundary space ("raw code.A second paragraph" defect at :2400); an empty body yields `""`.
   - `_blocks` (:970) — must unwrap `styled` (the v6y.7 regression at :959 that silently disabled every `limit:`); consecutive `item`s group into one block; `space`/`parbreak` are dropped.
   - `_tag-pred` (:438) — `none`, a bare string, `()` (no filter, NOT match-nothing), `match: "all"` vs `"any"`.
   - `_sort-ids` (:1612) — date-descending with undated last and ties ASCENDING by id (the reason it groups instead of sorting twice).
   - `_note-file` (:323) — path mirrors the handle `ideas:<slug>`.
   - `_bib-keys` (:217) — BibTeX `@type{key,` detection and the Hayagriva-YAML fallback, from `bytes` literals.
   - `_nest-outline` (:2243) — a flat `(depth:..)` run rebuilds the right tree, including a jump of more than one level.
3. Add to `rookery/0.2.0/Justfile`:
   test:
       typst compile --features html --root ../.. test/units.typ /dev/null
   (`--features html` is mandatory for `std.target` — see lib.typ:24-35. Use `--root ../..` so `/src/lib.typ` resolves, matching how `demo/pure` compiles.)
4. Keep `test/` out of the release archive — it already is: `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml` tars only `typst.toml`, `.marrow.typ` and `src/`.

NON-GOALS
Testing anything needing `state`/`context`/`query` convergence (`#idea`, `#window`, `_page-links`, `_ideas-outline-data`) — those belong to the demo-based beads, not here.

VERIFY
`cd rookery/0.2.0 && just test` exits 0. Then break one helper on purpose (e.g. make `_join` return `none` on empty) and confirm `just test` fails with a line number.

title: #search-bar's dropdown has no keyboard navigation
description:
PROBLEM
`rookery-search/0.2.0/src/lib.typ:313` emits the bar as an ARIA combobox — `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` wired at runtime — over a `role="listbox"` whose rows carry `role="option"` (`src/rookery-search.js:216`). Everything the pattern promises a keyboard user is therefore announced, and none of it works.

`wire` (:230) handles exactly two events: `input`, and `Escape` to clear. There is no ArrowDown/ArrowUp, no active-option tracking, no Enter-to-open, and `aria-selected` is never set on any row — grep confirms the only `aria-selected` writes in the file are in `wireModal` (:587, :590). So a reader who tabs into the bar and types gets a list they can only reach by tabbing through every option, with no indication of which is current, and a screen reader is told an option list exists that has no active option.

The modal (`wireModal`, :492) already implements all of this correctly: `select(i)` clamps without wrapping, sets `aria-selected`, mirrors it to a `data-rookery-search-selected` attribute for CSS, and calls `scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"})`; the keydown handler covers ArrowDown/ArrowUp plus Ctrl-n/Ctrl-p and Enter. This is a matter of extending that behaviour to the bar, not designing it.

STEPS
1. Factor the selection logic out of `wireModal` into a helper both callers use — it is the same job over a different container (`.rookery-search-results` vs `.rookery-search-list`) and a different follow-up action (the modal re-renders its preview; the bar does not). Pass the "on select" step in.
2. In `wire`, add a keydown handler: ArrowDown/ArrowUp (and Ctrl-n/Ctrl-p, matching the modal) move the selection with `preventDefault`; Enter navigates to the selected rows href; Escape keeps its current behaviour.
3. Set `aria-activedescendant` on the input to the selected rows id — the combobox pattern requires it, and unlike the modal (where focus is inside a dialog) the bars input keeps focus throughout, so it is the only way the current option is conveyed. That means rows need runtime-assigned ids; `wire` already assigns the listbox id this way (:239) for exactly the reason ids cannot live in the markup.
4. Reset the selection to none on every `render()`, so a fresh query does not inherit the previous querys index.
5. Style the selected row in `src/rookery-search.css` off `data-rookery-search-selected`, reusing the modals rule rather than adding a second one.

VERIFY
Keyboard-only in `demo/`: tab to the bar, type, arrow down and up through the results, confirm the highlight moves and stops at both ends without wrapping, and Enter opens the highlighted note. With a screen reader or the accessibility inspector, confirm the input reports an active descendant that tracks the highlight.

title: No JS tests for the browser-only half of rookery-search
description:
PROBLEM
`rookery-search/0.2.0/src/rookery-search.js` is 776 lines and there is no JavaScript test runner in the package at all — `package.json` has only a `build` script, and `test/parity.mjs` is a hand-rolled diff of two scorers. Everything with no Typst counterpart is therefore untested, including the fiddliest arithmetic in the package.

UNTESTED, IN ROUGH ORDER OF RISK
1. `snippet` (:145) — cluster-space anchor selection, `radius` window clamping, the `…` prefix/suffix, and `ranges` offsets that must account for the prefix. `wireModal` calls it with `radius = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (:523), which must yield the whole body and no ellipses.
2. `findClusterMatches` (:122) — overlapping and adjacent occurrences; an empty needle returns `[]`.
3. `matchRanges` (:326) — merging overlapping ranges; the length-preserving-`fold` assumption its comment rests on (:322).
4. `search` (:96) — tier boundaries and tie-breaks (see the tiering-parity bead; that one covers cross-language agreement, this one covers the JS side alone).
5. `extractNote` (:439) — needs a DOM. Feed it a `DOMParser`-parsed string of a minted-page shape: takes the elements between `h1.idea` and `footer.idea-footer`, carries the h1s `style` onto the wrapper, drops `<script>`, resolves relative `href`/`src` against the page URL, leaves `#fragment` links alone, and returns `null` both when there is no `h1.idea` and when the range is empty.

STEPS
1. Use the node built-in runner — no new dependency for 1-4: add `"test": "node --test test/"` to `package.json`, and `test:` to the `Justfile` beside `parity:`. Also add `"type": "module"` to `package.json` while there; node currently prints a MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning on every `just parity` run.
2. Test 5 needs a DOM. Either add `linkedom` as a devDependency (small, no browser) or use `node:test` with a minimal hand-built stub — prefer `linkedom`, since `extractNote` uses `querySelector`, `matches`, `nextElementSibling`, `importNode` and `URL` resolution, and a stub for that is more code than the test.
3. Leave `wire`/`wireModal`/`init` out of scope — they are event wiring over a real document and belong to a browser-level test, not this bead.

VERIFY
`cd rookery-search/0.2.0 && just test` passes. Break `snippet`s prefix accounting (`start: clippedStart - start` without `prefix.length`) and confirm a failure.

title: Hardcoded @rheo/rookery:0.2.0 in six places, no consistency check
description:
PROBLEM
The package spec `@rheo/rookery:0.2.0` is written out by hand in six places, and nothing checks any of them against the manifest that defines the version:

  rookery/0.2.0/.marrow.typ:72              — the real import; wrong here mints nothing
  rookery-search/0.2.0/src/lib.typ:21       — the cross-package dependency
  rookery/0.2.0/src/lib.typ:1419            — inside a panic message shown to authors
  rookery/0.2.0/src/lib.typ:785, :1586, :2516 — doc comments authors copy from

CI derives the release tag from `typst.toml` (`.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml` greps `name`/`version`), so cutting `rookery/0.3.0/` by copying the directory and bumping the manifest produces a release whose marrow still imports 0.2.0 — resolving to the OLD package if it is installed, and failing outright if it is not. The readmes carry version strings too.

STEPS
1. Add a `check-versions` recipe to the root `Justfile`. For each `<pkg>/<ver>/typst.toml`: read `name`/`version`, then assert that every `@rheo/<name>:<x.y.z>` occurrence anywhere under that directory (excluding `dist/` and `node_modules/`) names that same version, and that any `@rheo/<other>:<x.y.z>` names a version that exists as a directory in this repo.
2. Also assert the directory name matches the manifest `version` — the layout is `<name>/<version>/` per CLAUDE.md and nothing enforces it.
3. Wire it into the CI check workflow.
4. This is repo-wide, not rookery-specific: `slides`, `tooltip`, `justify`, `blogfeed` and `sidebar` carry the same strings in their readmes.

NON-GOAL
Templating the version out of the source. A Typst import spec has to be a literal, and a build step that rewrites `src/` would break `@rheo/rookery`s whole reason for being buildless (CLAUDE.md, "Pure-Typst packages"). A check is the right shape; a generator is not.

VERIFY
`just check-versions` passes on the repo as it stands. Change `rookery/0.2.0/.marrow.typ:72` to `:0.1.1` and confirm it fails naming that file and line.
